_readme: Every combat resource pool. Edit this file, then run Prince's Palace > Build Default Content. WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: mana used to be code -- a constant in Core (GameplayConstants.DefaultMaxMana = 30), a capacity chain in ContentDatabase.Effective, three colours in FightHudPalette, and an 'everyone has mana' assumption threaded through the fight. The owner's standing per-PC requirement is that a character can trade mana for a different resource, be forbidden spell books, and pay for skills in that resource -- none of which is expressible against code without one special case per switch. So mana became a row here, and a second resource is a second row rather than a parallel system. AT RUNTIME a pool is one clamped counter with a capacity, three gain triggers and a decay -- the same thing a character's signature resource already is (see Domain/Combat/ResourcePool.cs); what makes two pools feel different is which numbers are authored, not which code runs. TWO CAPACITY RULES, and the difference is the point: 'WisdomDerived' means the authored capacity is a BASE and every Max Mana source in the game (the Wisdom bonus from AbilityDerivation, talents, relics, the reward track, FlatMaxManaBonus) adds to it -- that is mana as it has always worked; 'Fixed' means the authored capacity is the WHOLE number from every source, which is what lets a resource promise '0..100, always' and have that be literally true rather than true until somebody equips a relic. HOW A NUMBER HERE REACHES A FIGHT: every combatant's CombatantState.PrimaryPool is built from the row its character's primaryPoolId names (ContentDatabase.BuildPrimaryPool), so capacity 30 is THE 30 -- the constant that used to sit beside it in code is gone. Under 'WisdomDerived' the authored capacity and gainPerTurn are BASES the derived sources add to; under 'Fixed' they are the whole number, which is what lets a bar promise '0..100, always'. mana's gainPerTurn is 0 and that does NOT mean mana stops regenerating: every point of mana regen is derived from Wisdom, gear, talents and the reward track and is added on top of this base, so authoring a number here would ADD to what a character already regenerates. Field-by-field documentation, defaults and valid enum values: docs/CONTENT_SCHEMA.md.

pools._comment: THE FLAT GAINS ARE 0 BECAUSE EACH OF BJORN'S THREE ROOT TALENTS IS A FURY ENGINE (docs/PLAN_BJORN_CONSTELLATIONS.md section 1, Phase 2): the Sentinel pays per hit taken, the Einherjar per damaging action, the Juggernaut per turn, and an engine REPLACES the flat gains for whoever holds it. A Bjorn with no root earns no Fury from swinging or being hit; the root is free and the pick is mandatory. decayPerIdleTurn stays the default an engine may override. THE REST OF THIS NOTE IS THE ORIGINAL FIRST-VALUE REASONING, kept for the shape it describes: gainOnAttack 15, gainOnDamageTaken 10 and decayPerIdleTurn 10 were picked to give the shape the owner asked for -- roughly three exchanges from empty to a spendable amount, and a bar that drains if Bjorn spends a turn doing something other than hitting or being hit -- and nothing has yet played a run against them. The balance pass that settles them is the same pass that authors what Fury BUYS: his slam and his brace are manaCost 0 today (see skills.json), because a Zero-start pool means he opens every fight unable to pay for anything, and pricing his kit before the income exists would have priced it against a guess. Run tools/bot.ps1 over the pair together, not either alone.
